question: A grants team is designing a new way of working in which Claude prepares the first draft of each funding decision summary. Nothing has been built yet. What should the team do first?
options: A) Agree what an acceptable summary contains, so drafts can be judged against it
B) Announce the new arrangement so that people begin sending their cases through
C) Write the longest and most detailed instruction the team can manage in one go
D) Ask every member of the team to try their own approach and compare next month
correct_answers: A) Agree what an acceptable summary contains, so drafts can be judged against it
explanations: Correct. Defining what "good" looks like before delegating is what makes every later round of iteration meaningful; without it, nobody can say whether a draft is acceptable or whether a change helped.
Announcing an arrangement that has not been designed pushes unfinished work onto colleagues and makes problems harder to withdraw from.
Instruction length is not the design. A long instruction written before the team knows what it wants encodes guesses at scale.
Four private approaches produce four private standards, and a month later there is still no agreed standard to compare them against.
